title: Thai Basil Chicken Wok Pancake
cScaleSummary: C3 because ground chicken and one whole egg contribute a moderate amount of dietary cholesterol across four servings. The herbs, aromatics, seasonings, panko, and cooking oil contribute little or no cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: Not LDL-Active because the recipe is centered on ground chicken rather than soluble-fiber-rich legumes, whole grains, or vegetables. Avocado oil and abundant fresh herbs keep the preparation relatively restrained in saturated fat, but that alone does not make it LDL-Active.
intro: This is not a traditional Thai dish, but its flavor structure borrows from Thai stir-fries built around fish sauce, chiles, garlic, and fragrant Thai basil. Instead of rolling seasoned ground chicken into meatballs, the mixture is pressed directly into a hot wok as one broad pancake. The technique creates a deeply browned crust before the chicken is divided, flipped, and broken into irregular pieces. A sharp lime-and-fish-sauce glaze and fresh basil finish the dish without softening that hard-earned sear.

items.prep: white and light-green parts finely sliced; dark-green parts reserved for finishing

miseEnPlace: Finely slice {{ingredient:scallions}}, keeping the dark-green parts separate for finishing.
Measure the remaining chicken-mixture ingredients and the {{ingredient:avocado-oil}}.
Combine {{ingredient:soy-sauce-finish}}, {{ingredient:fish-sauce-finish}}, {{ingredient:rice-vinegar}}, {{ingredient:lime-juice}}, and {{ingredient:sesame-oil-finish}} in a small bowl.

stepGroups.title: Mix the Chicken
items: Combine the {{ingredient:ground-chicken}}, the white and light-green parts of the {{ingredient:scallions}}, {{ingredient:garlic}}, {{ingredient:fresh-ginger}}, {{ingredient:fish-sauce-mixture}}, {{ingredient:soy-sauce-mixture}}, {{ingredient:sesame-oil-mixture}}, {{ingredient:white-pepper}}, {{ingredient:egg}}, and {{ingredient:panko}}. Mix just until evenly incorporated.
Fold in the {{ingredient:thai-basil-mixture}}. Let the mixture stand for 10 minutes while the panko hydrates.

stepGroups.title: Sear the Wok Pancake
items: Heat a large wok or 12-inch heavy skillet over medium-high to high heat until very hot. Add the {{ingredient:avocado-oil}} and swirl to coat the cooking surface.
Add the chicken mixture and immediately press it into one broad pancake about 3/4 inch thick. Cook undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes, until the underside develops a deep golden-brown crust.
Cut the pancake into 4 wedges with a wok spatula and flip each wedge individually. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the second side is browned and the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F.
Break the wedges into large irregular pieces. Let the newly exposed surfaces contact the hot wok for 1 to 2 minutes to pick up additional browning.

stepGroups.title: Glaze and Finish
items: Reduce the heat to low. Add the prepared finishing sauce a little at a time, tossing just until the chicken is lightly glazed; do not add so much that the browned crust becomes wet or soft.
Remove from the heat and finish with {{ingredient:jalapeno}}, the reserved dark-green parts of the {{ingredient:scallions}}, and {{ingredient:thai-basil-finish}}. Serve immediately.
